prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down indoor salon layout where the camera wearer stands above and directly in front of a seated person reclining backward into a washbasin on the right, with a tiled floor and another chair below on the left (~1.0–1.5 m away). The camera wearer's arms and hands in the lower foreground are the closest surfaces (~0.2–0.5 m), reaching into the basin (~0.5–0.7 m away) to touch the reclining person's head (~0.4–0.6 m away, within arm's reach), while the person's torso, crossed hands, and legs extend downward and to the left (~0.8–1.3 m away). Across the five frames, the camera wearer's left hand moves from left of the basin in frame 1, down toward the neck in frames 2–3, over the person's face in frame 4 (occluding it), and back to the head in frame 5, while the right hand stays near the basin rim and sprayer hose on the right. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the vertical layering of the camera wearer's foreground arms, the elevated basin and head, and the receding chair and floor below. However, the depth map is unreliable over privacy-blurred regions in frames 1, 2, and 5—where it hallucinates a smooth, bright convex dome over the blurred face—and in frame 3 where pixelation flattens the depth of the reclining person's legs and completely misses the standing person in the upper left (~1.8–2.2 m away).
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map labels only a sparse subset of foreground regions in the salon scene, grouping the reclining person (~0.4–1.3 m in front of and below the camera wearer, facing upward toward the ceiling and camera wearer) and the camera wearer's own arms (~0.2–0.5 m at the bottom edge) into overlapping 'person' masks. In frame 3, it additionally detects a second standing person at the upper left (~1.8–2.2 m away, ~1.0 m left of the seated person, partly cut off by the top frame edge) carrying a small container within their arm's reach, before that person exits the view in frame 4. Across the five frames, the masks shift as the camera wearer's arms reach across the reclining person's head and the basin on the right, with the camera wearer's left arm occluding the reclining person's head in frame 4. While segmentation helps isolate the distant upper-left bystander in frame 3 and separates the camera wearer's lower torso/arms from the reclining person in frame 3 more distinctly than a quick glance at the pixelated RGB, it is largely unreliable throughout the strip. It merges the reclining person and the white ceramic sink into a single 'person' mask in frames 1, 2, and 5, drops most of the seated person's body in frame 4, and misclassifies the chair armrest as a 'cell phone' in frame 1 (~0.7 m away on the lower left) and the sink's sprayer hose as a 'spoon' in frame 4 (~0.6 m away on the right).
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders sparse 2D skeletal keypoints on black, capturing only isolated hands and partial upper-body links within the salon scene while omitting all background objects like the sink and chairs. In frames 1, 2, and 4, only a single magenta hand skeleton is detected for the camera wearer's left hand (~0.3–0.5 m away on the left in frame 1, shifting down near the bottom-left edge in frame 2) or right hand (~0.5 m away at the lower right of the basin in frame 4, within arm's reach of the sprayer). In frame 3, where the face is unblurred, a yellow upper-body and head skeleton appears for the reclining person (~0.5–1.0 m in front of and below the camera wearer), showing their head tilted back on the right facing upward toward the camera wearer, their torso angled toward the upper left, and their hands clasped over their abdomen (~0.8 m from the camera wearer), overlapped by a magenta hand skeleton of the camera wearer at the bottom center. In frame 5, a distorted yellow torso box is detected on the reclining person's chest/lap area (~0.8–1.0 m away on the left) without head or limb keypoints. Although pose keypoints in frame 3 make the reclining person's upward head orientation and folded-arm posture explicit despite heavy RGB pixelation on their lower body, the map is highly unreliable across the sequence because privacy blurring and steep egocentric foreshortening cause total missed detections of the reclining person in frames 1, 2, and 4, the standing bystander in frame 3, and most of the camera wearer's own arms and hands.
